title: Top-N per Group reference solution
answer: WITH ranked_products AS (SELECT category_id, product_id, name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity) DESC) AS product_rank FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY category_id, product_id, name) SELECT * FROM ranked_products WHERE product_rank <= 3 ORDER BY category_id, product_rank;
explanation: The query returns the top ranked products per category, including ties at rank three. Review the query against the lab data and explain why the chosen joins, filters, aggregation grain, ordering, or transaction boundary is correct.
